Следующий шаг: до ближайшего цикла торгов разметить открытые заявки по составу конкурентов, ввести порог и продавать сервис отдельной строкой или многолетним контрактом, чтобы можно было ставить $3,000 за машину, не отдавая год обслуживания бесплатно.

**Источник:** `Darden 2019`, Copier Co., pp. 136–145 — Exhibit 2 (цены заявок $5,000 / $4,000 / $3,000; размеры заказов 20 / 25 / 30; себестоимость аппарата $3,000; сервис $0.05 за страницу; 1,000 страниц на копир в месяц; 'Service for 1 year included'); таблица Math Guidance, с. 142 (контрибуция на копир $2,000 / $1,000 / $0; сервис $600; прибыль на копир $1,400 / $400 / ($600); итог по контракту $28,000 / $10,000 / ($18,000)); clarifying information, с. 137 (побеждает наименьшая заявка, премия от объёма продаж, новый низкоценовой конкурент); brainstorm, с. 144 (менеджмент хочет участвовать во всех торгах); conclusion, с. 145. |

drills.anchor_metric: Порога у клиента нет — в кейсе напечатана только жалоба на падающую маржу ('the company has experienced declining profit margins'), никакой нормы прибыли или порога по сделке не задано. Значит закрывать вопрос сравнением с нормой нельзя: решает знак прибыли внутри сегмента и цена, ниже которой сделка не может быть безубыточной ($3,000 аппарат + $600 включённый год сервиса).

mehanizm.naive: складывает три разных типа торгов в один котёл и судит о бизнесе по общей цифре
mehanizm.correct: разбирает пул по составу конкурентов и смотрит на сегмент, который один уходит ниже себестоимости
mehanizm.why: средняя по 75 копирам положительна только потому, что две прибыльные колонки перекрывают третью; третья не «менее выгодна», она структурно убыточна — при цене $3,000 контрибуция на аппарат ноль, а включённый год сервиса в $600 отдан бесплатно, и именно там самые крупные заказы, которые премирует схема оплаты продавцов

drills.family_note: круг 102: книга печатает три сценария торгов по составу конкурентов, и один из них уходит ниже себестоимости при нулевой контрибуции — решает не средняя по портфелю сделок, а именно этот крайний сегмент, и он же самый крупный по объёму заказа; это хвост, а не средний случай.

drills.title: The Two-Dollar Sponge
drills.prompt:
Norrfield Medical makes HemoSeal, a blood-clotting agent sold to hospitals in single-use liquid vials and applied during post-op with a sponge. Padwell, a sponge manufacturer, has proposed a hybrid product: Norrfield supplies HemoSeal in dry tablet form, Padwell builds the tablet into its sponge and sells the finished product to hospitals, taking on marketing and customer relationships. Norrfield's brief to us was to maintain or improve profitability.

An associate worked the deal economics and left the working note below. She is out sick, and the partner meets Padwell tomorrow.

Read her note and give the partner your verdict: what should Norrfield do about the Padwell deal, what in the note supports it, what could go wrong, and what happens next.

**Answer in one field. Mark the blocks yourself.**

exhibit.title: Associate's working note — Padwell hybrid, deal economics

lines: **Block A — What is being sold, and to whom**
Customers: 1,000 hospitals with operating rooms, throughout the U.S.
Today Norrfield sells HemoSeal to them in a liquid glass vial; a sponge is bought separately.
Under the proposal Norrfield sells the tablet to Padwell; Padwell takes care of marketing and customer relationships and sells the finished hybrid.

Buyer-side notes from the interviews: the hybrid enables greater efficiency in operating rooms; buyers prefer it because there is no need to make separate purchases of HemoSeal and sponge; there is no proven improved medical benefit.
All products are single use.
**Block B — Price I built for the hybrid**
Willingness to pay, original liquid vial: $85.
Willingness to pay, standalone sponge: $10.
WTP increases by 10% for the combined product.
So the hybrid prices at ($85 + $10) × 1.1 = $104.50.
**Block C — Norrfield's own per-unit costs, vial vs tablet**
**Block D — How the money splits if we hold our margin**
Padwell's sponge costs $2 to manufacture.
**Block E — Loose facts from the market scan, not yet worked in**
Norrfield owns the IP on HemoSeal.
There are no other companies that make a product like HemoSeal. It is not easy to replicate.
There is nothing especially unique about the sponges.
There are 10 large sponge makers.
**Open for tomorrow:** $83.50 holds our $80 and leaves Padwell $19. Padwell will push back on that. What number do we walk in with?

key.naive: **Naive path — the honest first answer.** The note ends on a lopsided split — $80 to us, $19 to the partner who has to market the thing — and on a question about a number, so the reader answers the question that was asked: shave the transfer price below $83.50 until Padwell has enough margin to push the product, and sign. It is honest because both sides do clear a profit at $83.50 and the hybrid does raise what the hospital pays from $85 to $104.50. It is also a decision to hand a slice of a book-verified $80 to a counterparty, taken without ever asking what that counterparty is being paid for.
key.decoy: **The tempting second branch — walk away and keep the vial.** Since Norrfield's margin is $80 either way, the hybrid looks like effort for nothing: refuse Padwell, keep selling the vial at $85 on $5 of cost. It reads as the disciplined answer and it protects the $80 — but it leaves on the table the same $19 the first branch was preparing to give away, and it does so while the note itself shows the $19 sits on a $2 input.
key.support: **What decides it, and it is who owns the scarce side against who owns the commodity side.** Block E, which the note never worked in, says HemoSeal cannot be replicated and Norrfield owns its IP, while the sponge has nothing unique about it and ten large makers produce it — and Block D prices that sponge at $2. So the transfer price is not the lever: at any number between $83.50 and lower, it only slides the same $19 between two parties. The lever is the $2 input. Norrfield can buy sponges outright — from Padwell or from any of the ten — and sell the hybrid itself: $104.50 − $3.50 − $2.00 = $99.00 per unit, against the $80.00 it earns today. The $19 the note was preparing to negotiate over is exactly the $19 that ownership captures.
key.risks: Internal: the deal was partly a way to get marketing and customer relationships, which Padwell was to take on — Norrfield has no such channel to the 1,000 operating-room hospitals today, so sourcing the sponge itself means building or buying that commercial capability, and the tablet's own sales & marketing line is only $0.50 against the vial's $1.50. External: the whole $104.50 rests on a 10% WTP uplift bought by convenience alone — the interviews record no proven improved medical benefit — so hospital purchasing can refuse the premium and pull the hybrid back toward the $95 the two products fetch separately.
key.next: Before tomorrow's meeting, do not table a transfer price. Within two weeks price the two ownership routes side by side — a supply contract for sponges at the $2 manufactured cost versus acquiring one of the ten large sponge makers — and in parallel test the $104.50 against a purchasing panel drawn from the 1,000 hospitals, since no proven medical benefit backs the 10% uplift.

en: Minto: the first sentence is the verdict itself, an action with a subject. A correct verdict arriving after the facts fails this line.
Says Norrfield should not sign on the note's terms — rejects the transfer price as the instrument rather than merely adjusting it.
Names the asymmetry in Block E: HemoSeal cannot be replicated and its IP is owned, while the sponge is unremarkable and made by 10 large makers at $2.
Gives the number that decides: $99.00 per unit if Norrfield sources the sponge itself, against $80.00 today, and ties that $19 to the $19 the note was about to negotiate away.
Does not settle for keeping the vial at $80 as the answer.
Gives one internal and one external risk.
Gives a specific, time-bound next step instead of a price to walk in with.
ru: Минто: первое предложение — сам вердикт, действием и с субъектом. Верный вывод после фактов не засчитывается.
Сказано, что Norrfield не подписывает на условиях записки — цена передачи отвергнута как инструмент, а не просто подкручена.
Названа асимметрия из блока E: HemoSeal не воспроизводится и IP наш, губка ничем не примечательна и её делают 10 крупных заводов по $2.
Дано решающее число: $99.00 за единицу, если губку берём себе, против $80.00 сегодня, и эти $19 связаны с теми $19, которые записка собиралась выторговывать.
Кандидат не остановился на «оставим флакон за $80» как на ответе.
Назван один внутренний и один внешний риск.
Дан конкретный следующий шаг со сроком вместо цены, с которой идти на встречу.

reference.en:
| field | text |
|---|---|
| **answer** | **Norrfield should not sign the Padwell deal on the note's terms; it should own the sponge instead — buy sponges outright from Padwell or acquire one of the ten large sponge makers — and sell the hybrid itself.** The note spends its whole page on the transfer price, but that price is not the lever: at $83.50 we hold $80.00 and Padwell keeps $19.00, and any number below it simply hands part of a $80.00 margin to a partner whose contribution costs $2.00 to make. Block E, which the note never worked in, is what decides: HemoSeal cannot be replicated and we own its IP, while there is nothing especially unique about the sponges and 10 large makers produce them. Owning that $2.00 input leaves us $104.50 − $3.50 − $2.00 = $99.00 a unit against the $80.00 we earn today — the extra $19.00 is precisely the $19.00 we were preparing to negotiate away. Risks: internally, Padwell was to take on marketing and customer relationships, and we have no channel of our own to the 1,000 operating-room hospitals — the tablet carries only $0.50 of sales & marketing against the vial's $1.50 — so we must build or buy that capability; externally, the entire $104.50 rests on a 10% willingness-to-pay uplift bought by convenience alone, with no proven improved medical benefit recorded in the interviews, so hospital purchasing can refuse the premium and pull the price back toward the $95 the two products fetch separately. Next steps: table no transfer price tomorrow; within two weeks price the two ownership routes side by side — a supply contract for sponges at the $2.00 manufactured cost versus acquiring one of the ten large sponge makers — and in parallel test the $104.50 with a purchasing panel drawn from the 1,000 hospitals before any price is committed. |

**Source:** `6.-Wharton-Casebook-2017`, Medical Devices Co., pp. 170–175 — prompt and deal structure p. 170; clarifying answers (Spongy's takes marketing and customer relationships) p. 171; customers, benefits, WTP $85 / $10 / +10% / $104.5, sponge $2, margins $80 / $83.50 / $19, IP and uniqueness p. 172; per-unit cost table, vial $5.00 and tablet $3.50 p. 173; 10 large sponge makers and no replicable competitor p. 174; conclusion and vertical integration p. 175. $99.00 = $104.50 − $3.50 − $2.00 and $95 = $85 + $10 are arithmetic on those book inputs.
reference.ru:
| поле | текст |
|---|---|
| **ответ** | **Norrfield не подписывает сделку с Padwell на условиях записки: компания забирает губку себе — покупает её напрямую у Padwell или приобретает один из десяти крупных заводов — и продаёт гибрид сама.** Записка целиком ушла в цену передачи, но эта цена не рычаг: при $83.50 мы держим $80.00, Padwell оставляет себе $19.00, и любое число ниже просто отдаёт часть маржи в $80.00 партнёру, чей вклад стоит $2.00 в производстве. Решает блок E, который записка так и не встроила: HemoSeal не воспроизводится и IP принадлежит нам, тогда как в губках нет ничего особенного и их делают 10 крупных заводов. Владение этим входом за $2.00 оставляет нам $104.50 − $3.50 − $2.00 = $99.00 за единицу против сегодняшних $80.00 — лишние $19.00 это ровно те $19.00, которые мы собирались выторговывать. Риски: внутренний — на Padwell вешали маркетинг и работу с клиентами, а собственного канала к 1 000 госпиталей с операционными у нас нет, в таблетке заложено лишь $0.50 на sales & marketing против $1.50 во флаконе, значит канал придётся строить или покупать; внешний — все $104.50 держатся на надбавке к готовности платить в 10%, купленной одним удобством, и в интервью зафиксировано, что доказанной медицинской пользы нет, поэтому закупки госпиталей могут отказаться от премии и утянуть цену обратно к $95, которые два продукта дают по отдельности. Следующие шаги: завтра не выкладывать никакой цены передачи; за две недели просчитать два маршрута владения рядом — контракт на поставку губок по себестоимости $2.00 против покупки одного из десяти крупных заводов — и параллельно проверить $104.50 на закупочной панели из тех же 1 000 госпиталей до того, как цена будет зафиксирована. |

**Источник:** `6.-Wharton-Casebook-2017`, Medical Devices Co., стр. 170–175 — промпт и структура сделки стр. 170; уточняющие ответы (Spongy's берёт маркетинг и клиентов) стр. 171; клиенты, выгоды, WTP $85 / $10 / +10% / $104.5, губка $2, маржи $80 / $83.50 / $19, IP и уникальность стр. 172; таблица удельных затрат, флакон $5.00 и таблетка $3.50 стр. 173; 10 крупных производителей губок и отсутствие воспроизводимого конкурента стр. 174; вывод и вертикальная интеграция стр. 175. $99.00 = $104.50 − $3.50 − $2.00 и $95 = $85 + $10 — арифметика на этих книжных входах.

drills.anchor_metric: Формального порога клиент не назвал: заказ звучит как «сохранить или улучшить прибыльность». Записка молча сделала порогом сегодняшнюю маржу $80 за флакон — как база сравнения она валидна, как критерий согласия на сделку нет: удержать $80 можно и не подписывая.

mehanizm.naive: Маржи перекошены — сбиваю цену передачи ниже $83.50, чтобы партнёру хватило мотивации продавать, и подписываю сделку.
mehanizm.correct: Не подписывать на условиях записки: губка стоит $2 и её делают десять взаимозаменяемых заводов, поэтому Norrfield берёт губку себе и оставляет $99.00 вместо $80.00.
mehanizm.why: Цена передачи только перекладывает одни и те же $19 между двумя сторонами и потому не меняет положения Norrfield по существу. Торгуясь за неё, кандидат молча принимает, что дистрибуцию и губку обязательно надо покупать у партнёра, — тогда как та же записка в блоке E показывает, что дефицитен один HemoSeal, а губка воспроизводима десятью заводами по $2.

drills.family_note: круг 102: записка целиком стоит на цене передачи $83.50 — самой громкой величине страницы, — но эта цена лишь делит $19 между двумя сторонами; рычаг в том, кто владеет губкой за $2, которую делают десять взаимозаменяемых заводов.

drills.title: Saving On The Sickest
drills.prompt: A colleague on the disease-management team left the working note below before going on leave. The payer is first to market with the programme and is now deciding which population to go out and acquire. Read the note and tell the client what to do. **Answer in four fields: conclusion, supporting facts, risks, next step.**

exhibit.title: Associate's working note — disease-management programme economics

lines: **Block A — the programme as designed**

The payer covers 5 million members. A Health Coach works remotely by phone and email, contacts 8 members per day, 25 days per month, and carries one portfolio continuously. Annual cost per Coach is $60K salary plus 20% other — training, benefits, laptop. There are no other programme costs. Published studies show that once-a-month contact with a patient reduces that patient's health spending by 5%, on average.
Portfolio size: 8 x 25 = 200 members per Coach.
Cost per Coach: $60,000 + 20% = $72,000 per year.
**Block B — where the members sit**
20% of members are 65+ (Medicare Advantage; premiums funded by government). 40% of the 65+ population carries diabetes. Sized against that population, full coverage needs 2,000 Coaches.

header: Average diabetic, multiple of segment average

lines: The 4x figure is printed for the Group row only. I have carried the ×4 diabetic multiple across all three segments in the arithmetic below.
**Block C — what one Coach returns on 65+ diabetics**
A 65+ diabetic runs at $300 x 4 = $1,200 PMPM. At a 5% saving that is $60 per member per month, $720 per member per year.
One portfolio: $720 x 200 = $144K of saving a year, against a $72K Coach. Profit is $72K per Coach — two times the cost of a Coach.
Across 2,000 Coaches: $144MM per year.
**Block D — the other two segments, same arithmetic**
Individual: $150 x 4 = $600 PMPM, 5% = $30 per member per month, $360 a year. One portfolio returns $72K against a $72K Coach — break-even.
Group: $100 x 4 = $400 PMPM, 5% = $20 per member per month, $240 a year. One portfolio returns $48K against a $72K Coach — a $24K loss. 650K Group diabetics stay uncoached.
**Block E — the question on the table**

The client is first to market and plans to take the Health Coach programme outside its own book. The 65+ diabetic is where the programme yields the greatest saving by a wide margin — $720 a member a year against $360 for Individual and $240 for Group. Marketing the plan to that population is the obvious growth move, and the sales team is already drafting it.
I have not written the recommendation.

key.naive: **Naive path — the honest first answer.** Go after 65+ diabetics. Every line of the note holds: a coached 65+ diabetic returns $720 a year, three times the Group diabetic and twice the Individual, and one Coach clears $72K over cost — a two-times return, $144MM a year across the segment. If the programme is the asset, grow the population it works best on, and the $144MM becomes the proof point in the pitch. An experienced person lands here in thirty seconds and is not being careless.
key.decoy: **The tempting second branch — go and rescue the 650K uncoached Group diabetics.** The note leaves them sitting at a $24K loss per portfolio, and there are real ways to close it: coaching at the workplace, bi-monthly instead of monthly contact, automated correspondence, an employer fee. It deserves a sentence. But it is margin repair on members the plan already carries and already pays claims for; it is not an answer to the question the client asked, which is whom to go out and acquire.
key.support: **What decides it, and it is the plan's cost of carrying the member against the saving the Coach makes on him.** The note priced one side of the 65+ diabetic and stopped there. Side one, written down: the Coach saves $720 a year on that member. Side two, never written down: that same member costs the plan $1,200 PMPM — $14,400 a year — and after the 5% saving still $13,680, against $3,600 a year for a 65+ member at the segment average of $300 PMPM. Every 65+ diabetic the plan recruits arrives with roughly four times the average claim cost of the segment and hands back $720. The programme lowers the price of a risk the plan is already obliged to pay for; it does not make that risk worth buying. The $144MM is real and it is retrospective — it is the saving on a population the plan already carries, not a margin on a population it could go and sell to.
key.risks: Internal: the entire $144MM rests on the 5% figure, which is a published average never tested on this plan's own book, and on a 200-member portfolio that is an assumption of the same kind — one pilot away from being wrong in either direction. External: the only external route that does not require the plan to underwrite the member's claims is selling the Coach service to other payers, and that is unpriced and runs straight into regulation and member-information sharing.
key.next: Run a 65+ diabetic pilot on the plan's existing book — 20 to 30 Coaches, two quarters — to prove the 5% saving and the 200-member portfolio before any Coach is hired at scale; in parallel, put a price on the Coach service sold to other payers, with legal on information sharing, and bring both to the next board cycle.

en: Minto: the first sentence is the verdict itself, an action with a subject. A correct verdict arriving after the facts fails this line.
The verdict separates the two uses of the programme: coach the diabetics the plan already carries, do not go and recruit more of them.
Names the number the note never wrote down — a 65+ diabetic costs the plan $1,200 PMPM, $14,400 a year, and still about four times the segment average after the 5% saving.
Sets the Coach's $720 a year against that carrying cost, not against the Coach's own $72K, and says out loud that the note compared the saving to the wrong thing.
Does not throw the programme away: the $144MM on the existing 65+ book stands and the recommendation keeps it.
At least two risks, one inside the plan (the unproven 5% and the 200-member portfolio) and one outside it (regulation and information sharing on selling the service to other payers).
Next step is dated, sized and owned — a pilot on the existing book before scale, and a price for the service sold to other payers.
ru: Минто: первое предложение — сам вердикт, действием и с субъектом. Верный вывод после фактов не засчитывается.
Вердикт разводит два применения программы: коучить диабетиков, которых план уже несёт, и не идти набирать новых.
Названо число, которого в записи нет: диабетик 65+ обходится плану в $1,200 PMPM, $14,400 в год, и после экономии в 5% остаётся примерно вчетверо дороже среднего по сегменту.
$720 экономии поставлены против стоимости содержания члена, а не против $72K коуча, и вслух сказано, что запись сравнила экономию не с тем.
Программа не выброшена: $144MM на существующей базе 65+ остаются в силе, и рекомендация их сохраняет.
Минимум два риска: внутренний (недоказанные 5% и портфель в 200 человек) и внешний (регулирование и обмен данными о членах при продаже сервиса другим плательщикам).
Следующий шаг с датой, объёмом и владельцем: пилот на существующей базе до масштабирования и цена сервиса для других плательщиков.

reference.en:
| field | text |
|---|---|
| **conclusion** | **We recommend keeping the Health Coach programme running on the 65+ diabetics the plan already carries, and not marketing the plan to 65+ diabetics as a growth segment.** |
| **supporting facts** | The note's return is right and it is a return on members we already pay for: $1,200 PMPM x 12 x 5% = $720 a member a year, $144K per 200-member portfolio against a $72K Coach, $144MM a year across 2,000 Coaches. What the note never priced is the member himself — a 65+ diabetic costs the plan $1,200 PMPM, $14,400 a year, and still $13,680 after the 5% saving, against $3,600 for a 65+ member at the $300 segment average. Recruiting that member buys roughly four times the average claim cost to collect $720. The programme lowers the price of a risk we already own; it does not make the risk worth buying. |
| **risks** | Internal: the 5% saving and the 200-member portfolio are both assumptions carried straight from published studies into a $144MM number, untested on our own book. External: the only external route that does not put us on the hook for claims — selling the Coach service to other payers — is unpriced and faces regulatory and member-information-sharing constraints. |
| **next step** | Two quarters, 20-30 Coaches, a 65+ diabetic pilot on the existing book to prove the 5% and the 200-member portfolio before scale; in parallel, a price and a legal read on selling the Coach service to other payers, both back at the next board cycle. |

**Source:** `Kellogg-2012`, Health Coaches, pp. 160–165 — 5 million members, 8 contacts x 25 days, $60K + 20%, 20% 65+, 40% diabetic, 2,000 Coaches, $144MM (case guide and math block, pp. 161–163); $150 / $100 / $300 PMPM and the 4x diabetic multiple (Exhibit #2, p. 165); "still almost 4x after savings" and the 650K uncoached Group diabetics (follow-up questions, p. 163).

| **вывод** | **Программу Health Coach оставляем на диабетиках 65+, которых план уже несёт, и не идём продавать план диабетикам 65+ как сегменту роста.** |
| **факты** | Возврат в записи посчитан верно — и это возврат по членам, за которых мы и так платим: $1,200 PMPM x 12 x 5% = $720 на человека в год, $144K на портфель в 200 человек против коуча за $72K, $144MM в год на 2,000 коучей. Чего запись не оценила — самого члена: диабетик 65+ обходится плану в $1,200 PMPM, $14,400 в год, и после экономии в 5% всё ещё $13,680 против $3,600 у члена 65+ по средней сегмента в $300. Набирая такого человека, мы покупаем счёт вчетверо выше среднего, чтобы собрать $720. Программа снижает цену риска, который у нас уже есть; она не делает этот риск выгодным для покупки. |
| **риски** | Внутренний: и 5% экономии, и портфель в 200 человек — допущения, перенесённые из чужих публикаций прямо в число $144MM, на собственной базе не проверенные. Внешний: единственный внешний путь, который не вешает на нас оплату счетов, — продажа сервиса другим плательщикам — не оценён по цене и упирается в регулирование и обмен данными о членах. |
| **следующий шаг** | Два квартала, 20-30 коучей, пилот на диабетиках 65+ на существующей базе — подтвердить 5% и портфель в 200 человек до масштабирования; параллельно цена и юридическая проработка продажи сервиса другим плательщикам; оба результата — к следующему совету. |

**Источник:** `Kellogg-2012`, Health Coaches, стр. 160–165 — 5 миллионов членов, 8 контактов x 25 дней, $60K + 20%, 20% 65+, 40% диабетиков, 2,000 коучей, $144MM (гайд и блок математики, стр. 161–163); $150 / $100 / $300 PMPM и множитель 4x (Exhibit #2, стр. 165); «still almost 4x after savings» и 650K неохваченных диабетиков Group (follow-up, стр. 163).

drills.anchor_metric: Порога у клиента нет: книга не задаёт ни целевой экономии, ни целевого возврата по программе. Единственная величина, похожая на порог, — стоимость коуча $72,000 в год, но это статья затрат самой программы, а не внешнее требование клиента. Вердикт держится на сравнении двух денежных потоков плана, а не на пороге.

mehanizm.naive: берёт сегмент, где программа экономит больше всего, и превращает его в цель для набора клиентов
mehanizm.correct: считает, во что плану обходится сам застрахованный, и ставит экономию коуча против его счёта, а не против стоимости коуча
mehanizm.why: $720 в год — это возврат по человеку, которого план и так обязан оплачивать; тот же человек приносит плану счёт в $14,400 в год, и 5% его не переворачивают — после экономии он остаётся примерно вчетверо дороже среднего по сегменту. Программа снижает цену уже принятого риска, а не делает риск выгодным для покупки.

drills.family_note: круг 102: первый эффект — экономия коуча на уже застрахованном диабетике — посчитан верно до последнего доллара; второй эффект, что каждый новый диабетик приходит в план со счётом вчетверо выше среднего по сегменту, переворачивает вывод о том, кого набирать.

drills.title: Half Of Every Visit
drills.prompt: The founders of a venture-backed biotech have an FDA-approved pill and no sales organisation of any kind. An associate has left the working note below on how the product should be sold. Give the founders your verdict. **Answer in two fields: conclusion first, then everything else.**

exhibit.title: Associate's working note — how we sell the compound

lines: **Block A — the company and the product**

The molecule cures Alzheimer's with 90% efficacy and has FDA approval. The company has never had a sales or marketing organisation — it has purely been a research firm to this point. Selling would be to neurologists and geriatric psychiatrists, not to the consumer of the product. No other firm will have a cure for the next five years.

Addressable market: 5MM users. Annual gross margin per user: $1,000. R&D to date: $1.5B, and the firm requires that R&D cost be recovered by Year 5 of the product — straight-line, $300MM a year. G&A: $25MM a year. Manufacturing and packaging are inside the gross margin.

rows: Percent of visit focused on our product
Annual fully loaded cost per sales rep

lines: **Block B — the five years, run on the contract column**
**Block C — where I got to**

Contract sales costs $12MM a year against $17MM for our own force. Because the contract rep gives our product half of each visit, I held coverage constant by buying 200k calls instead of 100k and 170 reps instead of 85; at $60 a call that still lands $5MM a year cheaper.
Both columns clear the Year 5 R&D recovery requirement and both are in the black from Year 2 — the $5MM does not change the shape of the P&L. On cost, contract wins.
I have not written the recommendation.

key.naive: **Naive path — the honest first answer.** Go contract. The arithmetic in the note is correct end to end: $12MM against $17MM, the half-attention problem already paid for by doubling calls and reps, both columns clearing the Year 5 R&D recovery, black ink from Year 2. Contract sales is a defensible landing point and the book itself calls it the correct approach once the owners decide not to sell the company. What makes the path naive is not the channel: it is closing the decision on the $5MM difference between two totals that bought different amounts of work — 100% of a visit on one side, 50% on the other — without ever settling whether doubling the calls repaired that. A candidate who lands on contract sales and names the definitional gap out loud has answered the question; one who lands on contract sales because $12MM is less than $17MM has not.
key.decoy: **The tempting second branch — pay the $5MM and build the own force anyway.** $5MM is 0.17% of the $3B of Year 5 gross margin, and a rep who gives the product his whole visit is plainly worth more than one who gives it half. The instinct is sound and the scale argument is right. But it is still an answer to the note's question. The note asked which of two sales forces to hire; nobody in this note asked whether Kestrel should be hiring a sales force at all.
key.support: **What decides it, and it is coverage-equivalence against a $5MM gap that is not decision-grade.** Two things move between the top and the bottom of the options table. First the unit changes: an own-force call is 100% of a visit, a contract call is 50%, and the note repairs that by buying twice the calls — which assumes two half-attention calls on a neurologist are worth one dedicated call. That is a claim about physician behaviour, not an arithmetic identity, and nothing in the note tests it; a contract organisation is typically less effective than an internal one, so the 200k calls almost certainly do not buy the coverage the 100k do. Second, the number the note decided on is $5MM a year — 0.17% of Year 5 gross margin of $3B, and small even against the Year 1 loss of $87MM. A gap that size cannot carry a channel decision. What can carry it is the fact sitting in Block A and used nowhere: the firm has never had a sales or marketing organisation. That makes the live options contract sales or selling the product to a firm that already calls on neurologists — and the second one is priced nowhere in this note.
key.risks: Internal: the firm has no commercial capability at all, so every number in the own-force column is a plan rather than an observed cost, and the 100k call requirement itself is unvalidated — build it wrong and the launch window, not the $5MM, is what is lost. External: the whole plan rests on the five-year clean run and on 60% penetration by Year 5 at $1,000 a user a year for a cure to an incurable disease; a competitor cure or payer pushback on that price moves the answer by orders of magnitude more than the channel choice does.
key.next: Before either sales contract is signed, put two things in front of the founders inside four weeks: a measured productivity comparison — what a contract rep at 50% share of voice actually converts against a dedicated rep, from the contract organisation's own book on comparable specialty launches — and indicative valuations from two large pharma buyers, so the founders choose between selling and staffing on numbers instead of choosing between two staffing lines.

en: Minto: the first sentence is the verdict itself, an action with a subject. A correct verdict arriving after the facts fails this line.

Does not close the channel on the $5MM: names it as 0.17% of the $3B Year 5 gross margin and small against the $87MM Year 1 loss. Choosing contract sales is fine — deciding it by that difference is not.
Names the unit that changed inside the table — 100% of a visit against 50% — and calls the doubling of calls an untested assumption about physician behaviour, not a repair.
Puts the option the note never priced on the table: the firm has never had a sales or marketing organisation, so selling the product or the company is a live branch.
Does not simply flip to the own sales force; the answer changes the question rather than picking the other column.
At least two risks, one internal (no commercial capability, own-force numbers are a plan) and one external (the five-year exclusivity window and the $1,000 price).
Next step is specific and time-bound and produces the two missing numbers: rep productivity and an indicative sale valuation.
ru: Минто: первое предложение — сам вердикт, действием и с субъектом. Верный вывод после фактов не засчитывается.

Не закрывает вопрос канала по $5MM: названо, что это 0,17% валовой маржи пятого года в $3B и мелочь против убытка первого года в $87MM. Выбрать контрактные продажи можно — решать по этой разнице нельзя.
Названа подмена единицы внутри таблицы — 100% визита против 50%, — и удвоение звонков названо непроверенным допущением о поведении врача, а не починкой.
На стол выложен вариант, который запись не оценивала: у фирмы никогда не было отдела продаж и маркетинга, значит продажа продукта или компании — живая ветка.
Ответ не сводится к «тогда берём свой отдел продаж»: он меняет вопрос, а не выбирает другую колонку.
Минимум два риска: внутренний (нет коммерческой функции, цифры своей колонки — план, а не факт) и внешний (пятилетнее окно без конкурента и цена $1,000).
Следующий шаг конкретен и датирован и добывает два недостающих числа: производительность представителя и индикативную оценку при продаже.

| **the rest** | The unit changed inside the options table and the note patched it instead of testing it. drills.anchor_metric: Порог у клиента есть и он экзогенный: «The firm requires that R&D costs be recovered by Year 5 of the product». Порог валиден, но выбор канала не решает — R&D возвращается в обеих колонках, и разница в $5MM его не двигает. В записи порог присутствует и уводит внимание в сторону.

mehanizm.naive: выбирает канал по разнице в итоговых затратах, не спросив, одинаковую ли работу покупают эти две суммы
mehanizm.correct: проверяет, что стоит за единицей сравнения — визит на 100% и визит на 50%, — и меряет разрыв в $5MM масштабом того решения, которое он якобы решает

К тому же $5MM — 0,17% валовой маржи пятого года: такая разница не выдерживает решения о канале, а настоящая развилка — нанимать продажи или продавать продукт тому, у кого они есть.

drills.family_note: круг 102: единица сравнения переопределяется внутри самой таблицы — «визит» в левой колонке отдан продукту на 100%, в правой на 50%, — аналитик чинит это удвоением звонков и к концу сравнивает две суммы, которые покупают разный охват, не заметив подмены.

drills.title: Seven Items Deep
drills.prompt: A manufacturer of retail display fixtures has watched its return on investment fall in each of the last three years. An associate has left the working note below and gone into the client meeting. The CEO wants your read before that meeting ends. **Answer in one field. Mark the blocks yourself.**

exhibit.title: Associate's working note — three-year ROI decline

lines: **Block A — three years of trading**

Revenue grew 25% over the three years, equally across both product types. The market grew 25% over the same three years; the client has remained the industry market share leader throughout and has maintained 25% market share. There are several players in the market but everything has remained stable from a competitive standpoint.
**Block B — capital employed**

No new investments in property, plant and equipment over the three years. Total working capital employed three years ago was $80M; today it is $130M. Inventory levels have increased by 300%, primarily in finished goods, from $25 million to $75 million. PP&E, receivables, payables and cash are all stable.
**Block C — what the company makes**
Custom displays, 50% of sales: produced only when an order is placed and the payment is received.
Standard displays, 50% of sales: manufactured to an open standard for display sizes and types and stored in inventory — built-to-stock.
The number of standardized products has increased from 5 to 12 over the last three years. 5 standardized products account for 80% of sales in standardized products.
**Block D — my reading**

ROI is net profit over capital employed, so I took the two halves in turn. The top half is clean: profit grew 25%, exactly in step with revenue, and cost of production held at 80% of revenue throughout — nothing is leaking on the P&L, and the business has kept pace with a market that grew at the same 25%. The bottom half is where the ratio is falling: PP&E has not moved, and the whole $50M increase in working capital is inventory, almost all of it finished goods.

So this is a planning failure on the built-to-stock half. We are carrying safety stock against a business 25% larger and reading the demand signal wrong — the stock has run away from the sales. The fix is a demand-forecasting programme across the standard line and a tighter safety-stock policy.
I have not written the recommendation.

key.naive: **Naive path — the honest first answer.** Run a demand-forecasting and safety-stock programme on the standard line. The note's diagnosis reads well and is not a straw man: profit is healthy, cost discipline is intact, PP&E is flat, the market and the client's share moved together, and the entire ROI decline sits in a $50M finished-goods build. Excess safety stock against a mis-read demand signal is a real cause and a standard remedy, and a competent operator would say it inside a minute.
key.decoy: **The tempting second branch — write down the obsolete stock and take the hit now.** Some of the $75M is out-of-date product that will never ship; clearing it restores the capital base immediately and is the fastest visible move on ROI. It belongs in the answer — but as a consequence, not as the answer. A write-off cleans the stock that already exists and does nothing about what refills the shelf next year, and it hits reported profit the moment it is taken, which is precisely why management will resist it.
key.support: **What decides it, and it is the tail of the product line against the typical item.** The note explains a 300% move with a 25% move and the two do not meet. Nothing on the trading side changed shape: revenue, market and share all grew 25% together, cost held at 80%, and the custom half — half the business — carries no inventory at all, because it is only produced after the order and the payment arrive. What did change in those three years is the count of standardized products: 5 became 12. Five of those twelve still account for 80% of sales in standardized products. The other seven carry the remaining 20% of half the business — on the order of a tenth of revenue — and each one of them demands its own finished-goods position, its own safety stock and its own obsolescence risk no matter how slowly it turns. The $50M went into the slow tail of the line, not into the fast items and not into growth. Better demand forecasting is a legitimate measure and the book lists it beside the other two without ranking them; the ranking is what the arithmetic supplies. Spread evenly across twelve items a forecasting programme treats the tail as if it were the average and leaves the structure that created the build standing, so it is the second move here and not the first. The first move that returns the capital is cutting the standard line back toward its top five, working down what is obsolete on the way out — and forecasting better on what remains.
key.risks: Internal: cutting the line means writing off or working down obsolete inventory, and the book says plainly that this will cause an immediate hit on profits, so management may be reluctant — in the same year the CEO is already explaining a falling ROI, so the profit hit and the ROI recovery have to be carried to the board in one conversation. Second risk, also internal: this case prints no external risk at all — market, share and competitive dynamics are stated as stable — so the other exposure to name is that a uniform forecasting programme run instead of the line cut leaves the SKU count that created the build in place. [Помета цеха, круг 102: книга внешнего риска не печатает; выдумывать его кандидату здесь нечем и не нужно.]
key.next: Within two weeks, pull finished-goods value, turns and obsolescence age for each of the twelve standardized products, and each item's revenue split by customer, so the cut is made with the customer exposure visible and not on the sales line alone. In parallel, size the write-down and the working-capital release so the CEO can put the profit hit and the ROI recovery in front of the board in the same paper.

en: Minto: the first sentence is the verdict itself, an action with a subject. A correct verdict arriving after the facts fails this line.

Prioritises rather than rejects: better demand forecasting stays a legitimate measure, but a programme spread evenly across all twelve items is the second move and the tail is the first. The arithmetic that carries the ranking: inventory up 300% against revenue up 25%.

Uses the two structural facts the note left unused — 5 standardized products became 12, and 5 of them still carry 80% of standard sales — to put the capital in the slow seven rather than across the line.
Notes that half the business carries no inventory at all, because custom displays are produced only after the order and the payment, so the whole build sits on one half.

Says what changes and in what order: cut the standard line back toward the top five first, with the forecasting and safety-stock work following on what remains rather than running evenly across all twelve.

Names the risk the case actually prints — writing off or working down the obsolete stock takes an immediate hit on profits, so management may be reluctant — and does not invent an external risk the note cannot support.
Next step is dated and produces the missing cut — finished-goods value and turns per SKU and revenue by customer behind each of the slow items.
ru: Минто: первое предложение — сам вердикт, действием и с субъектом. Верный вывод после фактов не засчитывается.

Расставляет приоритет, а не отвергает: улучшение прогнозирования остаётся законной мерой, но ровный проект по всем двенадцати позициям — второй ход, первый — хвост линии. Арифметика, которая держит этот порядок: запасы +300% против выручки +25%.

Использованы два структурных факта, которые запись оставила лежать: стандартных позиций стало 12 вместо 5, и первые пять по-прежнему несут 80% продаж сегмента — капитал сидит в семи медленных, а не размазан по линии.
Отмечено, что половина бизнеса запаса не держит вовсе: заказные дисплеи делают только после заказа и оплаты, значит весь прирост лёг на одну половину.

Сказано, что именно меняется и в каком порядке: сначала резать стандартную линию к первой пятёрке, а прогноз и настройка страхового запаса идут следом по тому, что осталось, а не ровным слоем по всем двенадцати.

Назван риск, который книга действительно печатает: списание или выработка устаревшего запаса бьёт по прибыли сразу, и менеджмент будет сопротивляться, — и не выдуман внешний риск, которого записка не выдерживает.
Следующий шаг датирован и добывает недостающий разрез: стоимость и оборачиваемость готовой продукции по каждому артикулу и выручка по клиентам за каждой медленной позицией.

reference.en:
| field | text |
|---|---|
| **answer** | **Halden should cut the standardized line back toward its top five products and work down the obsolete stock on the way out — better demand forecasting is the second move here, not the first.** **Why.** The note explains a 300% move with a 25% move. Revenue, the market and the client's share all grew 25% together and cost of production held at 80%, so nothing on the trading side changed shape; PP&E is flat and the whole $50M is finished goods. Half the business carries no inventory at all — custom displays, 50% of sales, are produced only after the order and the payment. What changed in three years is the line itself: 5 standardized products became 12, while 5 of them still account for 80% of sales in standardized products. The other seven carry the remaining 20% of half the business and each of them demands its own finished-goods position, safety stock and obsolescence risk however slowly it turns. The capital went into the tail of the line, not into growth. Better forecasting and tighter safety stock belong in the programme — the book lists them beside the line cut without ranking the three — but spread evenly across twelve items they treat that tail as the average and leave the structure standing, which is why they follow the cut rather than replace it. **Risks.** Internal: the write-down takes an immediate hit on profits, so management may be reluctant, in the same year the CEO is explaining a falling ROI — the profit hit and the capital release go to the board in one paper. Second risk, also internal: this case prints no external risk — market, share and competitive dynamics are all stated as stable — so the other exposure to name is that a uniform forecasting programme run instead of the cut leaves the SKU count that created the build in place. **Next step.** Inside two weeks: finished-goods value, turns and obsolescence age for each of the twelve standardized products, plus each item's revenue by customer so the cut is made with the customer exposure visible, and a sized write-down against the working-capital release. |

**Source:** `Kellogg-2012`, Tarrant Fixtures, pp. 69–72 — revenue $100M to $125M and +25%, cost of production stable at 80%, net profit $20M to $25M, no CAPEX, working capital $80M to $130M, inventory +300% from $25M to $75M primarily finished goods, custom and standard each 50% of sales, standardized products 5 to 12, 5 products = 80% of standardized sales, market +25% and 25% share held, competitive landscape stable (clarifying answers and key elements, pp. 70–71); the three fixes printed side by side and without priority — "Write-off or work-down obsolete inventory (this will cause an immediate hit on profits, so management may be reluctant)", "Improve demand forecasting to set more realistic safety stock levels", "Reducing the 'Standard' product-line down to the top 5 products (80% of current sales)" (solution, p. 72). The solution slide prints no external risk for this case.

| поле | текст |
|---|---|
| **ответ** | **Halden режет стандартную линию к первой пятёрке продуктов и по дороге вырабатывает устаревший запас — улучшение прогнозирования здесь второй ход, а не первый.** **Почему.** Запись объясняет движение в 300% движением в 25%. Выручка, рынок и доля клиента выросли на одни и те же 25%, себестоимость держалась на 80% — на торговой стороне форма не поменялась; PP&E не двигалось, и все $50M — готовая продукция. Половина бизнеса запаса не держит вовсе: заказные дисплеи, 50% продаж, делают только после заказа и оплаты. За три года изменилась сама линия: стандартных продуктов стало 12 вместо 5, при этом пять из них по-прежнему дают 80% продаж стандартного сегмента. Остальные семь несут оставшиеся 20% половины бизнеса, и каждая из них требует собственного склада готовой продукции, собственного страхового запаса и собственного риска устаревания — независимо от того, как медленно она оборачивается. Капитал ушёл в хвост линии, а не в рост. Прогнозирование и более тонкая настройка страхового запаса остаются в программе — книга перечисляет их рядом с сокращением линии и без приоритета, — но ровным слоем по двенадцати позициям они обращаются с хвостом как со средней позицией и оставляют структуру на месте, поэтому идут после сокращения, а не вместо него. **Риски.** Внутренний: списание бьёт по отчётной прибыли сразу, и менеджмент будет сопротивляться, — в тот же год, когда CEO объясняет падающий ROI; удар по прибыли и высвобождение капитала идут на совет одной бумагой. Второй риск тоже внутренний: книга внешнего риска по этому кейсу не печатает — рынок, доля и конкурентная картина объявлены стабильными, — поэтому вторая экспозиция в том, что ровный прогнозный проект, запущенный вместо сокращения, оставит породившее прирост число артикулов на месте. **Следующий шаг.** В две недели: стоимость готовой продукции, оборачиваемость и возраст запаса по каждой из двенадцати стандартных позиций, плюс выручка каждой позиции в разрезе клиентов, чтобы резать с видимой клиентской экспозицией, и посчитанный размер списания против высвобождения оборотного капитала. |

**Источник:** `Kellogg-2012`, Tarrant Fixtures, стр. 69–72 — выручка $100M → $125M и +25%, себестоимость стабильна на 80%, чистая прибыль $20M → $25M, отсутствие CAPEX, оборотный капитал $80M → $130M, запасы +300% с $25M до $75M преимущественно в готовой продукции, заказные и стандартные по 50% продаж, стандартных продуктов с 5 до 12, 5 продуктов = 80% продаж стандартного сегмента, рынок +25%, удержанные 25% доли и стабильная конкуренция (уточнения и ключевые элементы, стр. 70–71); три меры напечатаны рядом и без приоритета — «Write-off or work-down obsolete inventory (this will cause an immediate hit on profits, so management may be reluctant)», «Improve demand forecasting to set more realistic safety stock levels», «Reducing the “Standard” product-line down to the top 5 products (80% of current sales)» (решение, стр. 72). Внешнего риска слайд решения по этому кейсу не печатает.

drills.anchor_metric: Порога у клиента нет: клиент назвал только падающий ROI, ни целевого ROI, ни целевой оборачиваемости запасов книга не задаёт. Вердикт держится на разрыве темпов (+300% запасов против +25% выручки) и на структуре линии, а не на пороге.

mehanizm.naive: объясняет рост запасов ростом бизнеса и уходит чинить планирование ровным слоем по всей стандартной линии
mehanizm.correct: смотрит, что за три года изменилось в структуре линии — с 5 позиций до 12 при тех же 80% продаж на первой пятёрке, — и режет хвост, а не выравнивает прогноз по всем двенадцати
mehanizm.why: запасы выросли на 300% при выручке +25%: одним ростом такое не объясняется. Половина бизнеса запаса вообще не держит — заказные дисплеи делают после заказа и оплаты. Капитал ушёл в семь медленных артикулов, каждый из которых требует собственного склада независимо от того, как мало продаётся; ровный прогнозный проект обращается с хвостом как со средней позицией и оставляет структуру на месте. Прогнозирование при этом не отменяется — книга печатает его как одну из трёх мер без приоритета; приоритет задаёт арифметика, и прогноз идёт вторым шагом, после сокращения линии.

drills.family_note: круг 102: решает не типовая позиция стандартной линии, а её хвост — семь редко продающихся артикулов из двенадцати; пять первых по-прежнему несут 80% продаж сегмента, а хвост забрал почти весь прирост запасов в $50M. Средний артикул и средняя оборачиваемость тут не решают ничего.

drills.title: Payback On The Wrong Problem
drills.prompt:
Crossline Freight hauls freight across North America. For five years its costs have risen on the back of a driver shortage that pushed wages up, and the CEO wants operating costs down. An associate was asked to work up a hybrid tractor fleet — batteries plus diesel — and left this note before handing the file over. You have five minutes. Give your verdict on the note and tell the client what to do next.

**Answer in four fields: conclusion, supporting facts, risks, next step.**

exhibit.title: Associate's working note — hybrid tractor evaluation

lines: **Block A — What the client told us, in their words**
The goal is to bring operating costs down. There is no profitability target; the CEO says any improvement on where we are today counts.
The fleet runs at full capacity. The only thing capping revenue growth is finding drivers for the trucks we already own.
Revenue has risen steadily for five years and is capped by driver supply, not by demand.
Costs are up because wages are up — the whole industry is short of drivers and feels the same wage pressure. Fuel prices have also been rising steadily.
**Block B — Cost of operating each semi**
Fuel runs at an average of $3.00 a gallon. Depreciation is straight-line across the lifespan, $0 salvage at the end.
**Block C — What I have so far**
Fuel is where the hybrid wins. Standard: 60,000 miles ÷ 10 MPG = 6,000 gallons × $3.00 = $18,000 a year. Hybrid: 60,000 ÷ 20 = 3,000 gallons × $3.00 = $9,000 a year.
So $9,000 a year saved per truck on fuel. The hybrid costs $50,000 more to buy, which the fuel line alone pays back in about 5.6 years — inside a ten-year life, and the truck keeps saving after that.
Maintenance, insurance and depreciation all run higher on the hybrid. The figures are in the table above; I have not rolled them into a single number yet.
I have not written the recommendation.

key.naive: **Naive path — the honest first answer.** Take the note's frame and finish it: $9,000 a year of fuel against a $50,000 premium pays back in 5.6 years, well inside a ten-year life, and the truck goes on saving afterwards — so buy hybrids, and lean on the vendor and the insurer to make the case better still. Nothing the associate wrote is false, which is exactly why a strong reader signs it off; the question the note answers is simply not the client's question.
key.decoy: **The tempting second branch — improve the hybrid case.** Stretch the trucks past ten years, negotiate the $8,000 maintenance down, shop the $3,000 insurance, assume fuel keeps climbing — the client did say fuel prices have been rising steadily. Every one of these is a real lever. All of them are still an argument about which tractor to park in a yard whose trucks already run full, and none of them touches the constraint the CEO named.
key.support: **What decides it, and it is the client's stated constraint against the ledger in front of us.** Two things, in that order. First, close the arithmetic the note left open: the hybrid carries $5,000 more depreciation a year (($150,000 − $100,000) ÷ 10), $3,000 more maintenance and $1,000 more insurance. That is $9,000 — exactly the fuel saving. Annual cost per truck is identical on both columns, so the $50,000 premium is never repaid and the 5.6-year payback does not exist. Second, and this is the larger failure: the table has no line for the thing the client said is binding. The fleet is at full capacity, revenue is capped by driver supply, and the cost that has actually been rising is wages. A $50,000 premium per truck is capital committed to the asset that is not the constraint.
key.risks: Internal: the equality is not robust — the hybrid's maintenance is $8,000 against $5,000, and any drift in that line alone moves the answer; on top of that, driver wages may keep rising in a strong economy, and wages are the cost line that is genuinely growing. External: the whole comparison stands on $3.00 a gallon, so the hybrid's only advantage is a bet on the fuel price, and the wage pressure is industry-wide — every competitor is bidding for the same drivers.
key.next: Do not take the hybrid fleet to the capital committee on this analysis. Within two weeks, price the driver line: cost per driver-year, how many tractors sit idle for want of a driver, and the revenue those idle trucks would carry — then put driver-supply options (sign-on bonuses, part-time contract drivers in peak season, visa sponsorship for international drivers) against the same capital the fleet would have absorbed.

en: Minto: the first sentence is the verdict itself, an action with a subject. A correct verdict arriving after the facts fails this line.
The conclusion is about the client's constraint, not only about the trucks — it says what to stop and what to price instead.

Closes the arithmetic the note left open: +$5,000 depreciation, +$3,000 maintenance, +$1,000 insurance = $9,000, the same as the fuel saving, so annual cost is identical and the 5.6-year payback disappears.
Names the constraint printed in words — full capacity, revenue capped by driver supply, wages the cost that is rising — and states that no line of this table touches it.
Does not treat the missing saving as an arithmetic error by the associate: the note's fuel numbers are right, the frame is what fails.
At least two risks, one internal (maintenance drift, wage growth) and one external (the $3.00 fuel price the case rests on, industry-wide wage pressure).
Next step is specific and time-bound, and it is about drivers rather than tractor specifications.
ru: Минто: первое предложение — сам вердикт, действием и с субъектом. Верный вывод после фактов не засчитывается.
Вывод про ограничение клиента, а не только про грузовики: сказано, что остановить и что считать вместо этого.

Досчитана арифметика, которую записка бросила: +$5,000 амортизации, +$3,000 ремонта, +$1,000 страховки = $9,000, ровно экономия на топливе, поэтому годовая стоимость одинакова и окупаемости в 5.6 года не существует.
Названо ограничение, напечатанное словами — парк на полной загрузке, выручку держит нехватка водителей, растут зарплаты, — и сказано, что в таблице нет ни одной строки про это.
Отсутствие экономии не подано как арифметическая ошибка коллеги: числа по топливу верны, ломается рамка.
Минимум два риска: внутренний (разброс по ремонту, рост зарплат водителей) и внешний (цена топлива $3.00, на которой всё держится; отраслевое давление на зарплаты).
Следующий шаг конкретен и по срокам, и он про водителей, а не про характеристики тягача.

| field | text |
|---|---|
| **conclusion** | **Crossline should not take the hybrid fleet to the capital committee, and should move the next two weeks of work onto drivers: the hybrid saves nothing at all, and the constraint the CEO named has no line in this analysis.** |
| **supporting facts** | The fuel saving the note found is real and is exactly cancelled by the rest of the truck. Against the standard tractor the hybrid carries $5,000 more depreciation a year (($150,000 − $100,000) ÷ 10 years, straight-line to $0), $3,000 more maintenance ($8,000 vs $5,000) and $1,000 more insurance ($3,000 vs $2,000) — $9,000, precisely the $18,000 − $9,000 the hybrid saves on fuel at 60,000 miles and $3.00 a gallon. Annual cost per truck is the same on both columns, so the $50,000 premium is never repaid and the 5.6-year payback does not exist. Beyond the arithmetic: the client said the fleet already runs at full capacity, that the only cap on revenue growth is finding drivers, and that costs rose because wages rose. The table in front of us has no driver line at all, so even a genuine saving here would buy nothing against the binding constraint. |
| **risks** | Internal: the equality is thin — the hybrid's maintenance line is $8,000 against $5,000 and any drift in it moves the answer; and driver wages may keep rising in a strong economy, which is the cost line that is actually growing. External: the whole comparison stands on fuel at $3.00 a gallon, so the hybrid's case is a bet on the fuel price, which the client says has been rising steadily; and the wage pressure is industry-wide, so every competitor is bidding for the same drivers. |
| **next step** | Within two weeks, quantify the driver line: cost per driver-year, how many tractors sit idle for want of a driver, and the revenue those idle trucks would carry. Then price driver-supply options — sign-on bonuses, part-time contract drivers in peak season, visa sponsorship — against the same capital the hybrid fleet would have absorbed, and bring both to the same committee meeting. |

**Source:** `Darden 2019`, National Logistics, pp. 48–56 — Exhibit 1, p. 52 (purchase price $100,000 / $150,000; maintenance $5,000 / $8,000; insurance $2,000 / $3,000; 60,000 miles a year; 10 / 20 MPG; 10-year lifespan; fuel at $3.00 a gallon); Question 2, p. 53 (straight-line depreciation, $0 salvage; fuel $18,000 vs $9,000; $35,000 a year on both trucks); clarifying information, p. 49 (goal, no profitability target, full capacity, revenue capped by driver supply, industry-wide wage pressure, rising fuel prices); conclusion, p. 56 (risks: fuel prices, maintenance variation, driver wages); brainstorm, p. 55 (driver-supply options).
reference.ru:
| поле | текст |
|---|---|
| **вывод** | **Не выносим гибридный парк на инвесткомитет и переводим ближайшие две недели работы на водителей: гибрид не экономит ничего, а ограничение, которое назвал CEO, в этом расчёте вообще не представлено.** |
| **факты** | Экономия на топливе реальна и ровно съедается остальной машиной. Против стандартного тягача гибрид несёт +$5,000 амортизации в год (($150,000 − $100,000) ÷ 10 лет, линейно до нуля), +$3,000 ремонта ($8,000 против $5,000) и +$1,000 страховки ($3,000 против $2,000) — итого $9,000, ровно та экономия $18,000 − $9,000, которую даёт топливо при 60,000 миль и $3.00 за галлон. Годовая стоимость грузовика одинакова в обеих колонках, значит надбавка в $50,000 не возвращается никогда и payback в 5.6 года не существует. Дальше арифметики: клиент сказал, что парк уже работает на полную, что единственный ограничитель роста выручки — поиск водителей и что затраты выросли из-за зарплат. В таблице перед нами строки водителя нет вовсе, поэтому даже настоящая экономия здесь ничего не купила бы против связывающего ограничения. |
| **риски** | Внутренний: равенство держится на волоске — ремонт гибрида $8,000 против $5,000, и любой сдвиг этой строки переворачивает ответ; плюс зарплаты водителей могут продолжить расти при сильной экономике, а это и есть та статья, которая реально растёт. Внешний: всё сравнение стоит на топливе по $3.00 за галлон, то есть вся ставка гибрида — ставка на цену топлива, которая, по словам клиента, стабильно росла; и давление на зарплаты отраслевое — за тех же водителей торгуются все конкуренты. |
| **следующий шаг** | За две недели оцифровать строку водителя: стоимость водителя в год, сколько тягачей простаивает без водителя и какую выручку эти простаивающие машины принесли бы. Затем оценить варианты по предложению водителей — подъёмные при найме, контрактные водители на пик сезона, спонсирование виз — против того же капитала, который забрал бы гибридный парк, и вынести оба варианта на одно заседание комитета. |

**Источник:** `Darden 2019`, National Logistics, pp. 48–56 — Exhibit 1, с. 52 (цена $100,000 / $150,000; ремонт $5,000 / $8,000; страховка $2,000 / $3,000; 60,000 миль в год; 10 / 20 MPG; срок службы 10 лет; топливо $3.00 за галлон); вопрос 2, с. 53 (линейная амортизация, нулевая остаточная стоимость; топливо $18,000 против $9,000; $35,000 в год у обоих); clarifying information, с. 49 (цель, отсутствие целевого порога, полная загрузка, выручка ограничена водителями, отраслевое давление на зарплаты, рост цен на топливо); conclusion, с. 56 (риски: топливо, разброс по ремонту, зарплаты водителей); brainstorm, с. 55 (варианты по водителям).

drills.anchor_metric: Порога нет и это сказано прямо: 'Does the client have a profitability target? No, the client just wants to improve profitability from their current state'. Значит закрыть вопрос сравнением с нормой нельзя — решает то, двигает ли решение названное клиентом ограничение.

mehanizm.naive: принимает вопрос записки за вопрос клиента — окупается ли надбавка за грузовик экономией на топливе — и считает срок окупаемости

drills.family_note: круг 102: семья переставлена с F4 на F2 по ревью — тело решается досчётом брошенной арифметики (+$5,000 амортизации, +$3,000 ремонта, +$1,000 страховки = ровно $9,000 экономии на топливе, годовая стоимость обеих колонок одинакова), а неназванное ограничение по нехватке водителей работает второй опорой вердикта, а не решающей.

drills.title: The First Twenty Million
drills.prompt:
Alder Health Products makes an over-the-counter cough and cold medicine in a single ageing plant, where maintenance costs keep climbing and margins are thin. The choice is down to two: build a new facility beside the old one, or hand manufacturing to a contract manufacturer — who is also one of the two or three national players in the same category. An associate priced both and left this note. You have five minutes. Give your verdict.

**Answer in two fields: conclusion first, then everything else.**

exhibit.title: Associate's working note — make or buy

lines: **Block A — The decision as it stands**

One plant, ageing, with maintenance costs rising; that is what is holding margins down. The objective is to bring production cost down while holding product quality — cost, quality and brand image all matter to the buyer.

Two options left on the table: build a new facility next to the old plant, or outsource manufacturing to a contract manufacturer. There are two or three larger players with national distribution in this business and we are one of them; so is the manufacturer we would be handing production to. Everything we make is sold in the US.
**Block B — What each option costs, as quoted**

rows: Buy — total cost per bottle, first 20M bottles (regardless of total order size)
Buy — total cost per bottle, bottles after the first 20M (regardless of total order size)

lines: **Block C — What I have so far**
This is a large-volume decision, so the rate that matters is the one we pay on the marginal bottle: $2.50.

On that basis the bought margin is $4.50 − $2.50 = $2.00 a bottle, against $4.50 − $2.00 = $2.50 in our own plant. Building buys us $0.50 a bottle and costs $50M up front, so the two lines cross at $50M ÷ $0.50 = 100M bottles a year. Above that volume, build; below it, buy.
I have not written the recommendation.

key.naive: **Naive path — the honest first answer.** Accept the marginal-rate convention — pricing a make-or-buy off the marginal unit is the standard shortcut at scale — and work from 100M bottles: hold the volume forecast against it, build above, buy below. The convention is defensible in the abstract and the arithmetic on top of it is clean, which is why an experienced reader signs it off rather than reopening it.
key.decoy: **The tempting second branch — the counterparty.** The contract manufacturer is one of two or three national players in our own category, and quality and brand image are stated purchase drivers, so the reader argues that outsourcing to a direct rival is unacceptable whatever the arithmetic says. It is a real exposure and it belongs in the risks. It is not what the note got wrong, and putting it in the verdict leaves the $50M number standing on a crossover that is off by 10M bottles.
key.support: **What decides it, and it is the quoted schedule against the marginal rate.** Both ways of counting are defensible in general; here the quote itself settles which one applies. The first 20M bottles are $2.25 'regardless of total order size' — the cheap tier does not dissolve as the order grows, so it is a permanent $0.25 × 20M = $5M a year in favour of buying, and the marginal-rate shortcut throws all of it away. Put it back: $2.50x − $50M = $2.00(x − 20M) + $2.25 × 20M, so $2.50x − $50M = $2.00x + $5M, $0.50x = $55M, x = 110M bottles a year. Between 100M and 110M the note's rule says build and the quoted terms say buy — a $50M commitment landing on the wrong side of the line.
key.risks: Internal: the $2.00 in-house cost per bottle is exactly the number an ageing-plant business has just failed to hold, and if the new facility lands above it the crossover moves further out of reach. External: the contract manufacturer is one of the two or three national players in the same category, and quality and brand image are stated purchase drivers — handing production to a direct rival is a strategic exposure that no unit cost in this table prices.
key.next: Before the plant goes to the board, put the volume forecast next to 110M bottles a year rather than 100M, and have the contract manufacturer confirm the tiered schedule in writing for the length of the comparison — the whole $5M sits on that one clause.

en: Minto: the first sentence is the verdict itself, an action with a subject. A correct verdict arriving after the facts fails this line.
Names the convention that was swapped — the marginal rate in place of the quoted tiered schedule — rather than saying the note 'made a mistake'.
Quotes the clause that settles it: the first 20M bottles hold at $2.25 regardless of total order size, so the cheap tier never disappears.
Prices the discarded tier: $0.25 × 20M = $5M a year, permanently in favour of buying.
Gives the corrected crossover, 110M bottles a year, and shows the line that produces it rather than asserting it.
Says what the error costs: between 100M and 110M the note flips a $50M decision the wrong way.
Keeps the counterparty concern (outsourcing to a direct rival, with quality and brand image as purchase drivers) in the risks, not in the verdict.
ru: Минто: первое предложение — сам вердикт, действием и с субъектом. Верный вывод после фактов не засчитывается.
Названа подменённая конвенция — предельная ставка вместо объявленной ступенчатой схемы, — а не «коллега ошибся».
Процитирована оговорка, которая решает спор: первые 20M бутылок остаются по $2.25 при любом размере заказа, то есть дешёвая ступень не исчезает.
Оценён выброшенный транш: $0.25 × 20M = $5M в год, постоянно в пользу закупки.
Дана исправленная точка пересечения — 110M бутылок в год — и показана строка, из которой она получается, а не просто объявлено число.
Сказано, чем ошибка платится: на интервале 100M–110M записка разворачивает решение на $50M в обратную сторону.
Опасение по контрагенту (отдаём производство прямому конкуренту при том, что качество и бренд — драйверы покупки) стоит в рисках, а не в выводе.

drills.title: The Superstore Winter
drills.prompt:
You are the engagement manager on a diligence for an investor looking at a US branded office products manufacturer. The year is 1992. An associate spent the week inside the client's finance, sales and manufacturing functions and left you the working note below ahead of tomorrow's investment committee.

The note is honest work and it is unfinished — the associate stopped before writing a recommendation.

The team has two weeks left on the ground. Read the note and give your verdict: where do those two weeks go, and what do you tell the investor about this business?

**Answer in one field. Mark the blocks yourself.**

exhibit.title: Associate's working note — branded office products manufacturer, 1992 diligence

lines: **Block A — The client as it stands**
1991 sales $275m. Pre-tax profit currently $25m per year.
Five autonomous divisions sharing manufacturing and marketing functions. Shared costs are 45% of total and are allocated on a percentage-share-of-sales basis.
Grown through product line extensions and four key acquisitions. Carries 12,500 SKUs against 4,000-5,000 for competitors. Highest selling product is a high-end branded stapler.
Distribution: 75% wholesalers, 15% superstores, 10% end customers. Staples, Inc. is the largest single customer.
Three plants, current capacity utilization 50%.
Publicly traded, strong balance sheet, little long-term debt, weakening earnings. Analysts have the company down as an acquisition target.
**Block B — Top line and bottom line, same twelve years**
**Block C — The market over the same window**
The US office supplies market grew at a 5% CAGR historically. In 1990 and 1991 the market declined at 5% per year.
The superstore channel has gained 10 share points in the past two years and typically discounts products 30% to small retailers and dealers.
Superstores are aggressively substituting private label products for traditional brand names.
**Block D — Plant footprint, in SKUs**
**Block E — Plant operating costs, annual**
**Block F — My read so far**
Revenue carried per SKU is $275m / 12,500 = $22k.
The bottom line is falling roughly five times faster than the top line, and the top line is falling with the market.

Every account conversation I had this week came back to the same two things. Superstores discount 30% into the dealer base we sell through, and they are putting private label into shelf space our brands used to hold. The channel moved under us in twenty-four months and we did not move with it. That is where the money went.
I have not written the recommendation.

key.naive: **Naive path — the honest first answer.** Spend the two weeks on the demand side. The note argues it well: the market turned from +5% a year to -5% a year, superstores took 10 share points in twenty-four months, they discount 30% into the dealer base that carries 75% of our volume, and they are swapping private label into our shelf space. Sales fell at an 8% CAGR and profit at 40%. So the work is channel and price — rebuild the superstore terms, defend the branded stapler against private label, rethink the wholesaler discount ladder. This is what an experienced person says first, and every fact in it is true. It fails on one thing: not a single one of those quantities belongs to the client. The market's direction, the superstores' 10 points, their 30% discount and their private label push are all conditions, not levers. Two weeks spent there produce a story, not a decision the investor can price.
key.decoy: **The tempting second branch — prune the SKU tail.** The note hands you $22k of revenue per SKU and a 12,500 SKU count against 4,000-5,000 for competitors, so the branch computes cleanly: cut the tail, carry less complexity, look like the competition. It is the wrong shape of move on its own. Cutting SKUs surrenders $22k of revenue each and releases nothing, because the cost sitting under those SKUs is a plant footprint, not a SKU count — three plants at 50% utilization keep their fixed costs whatever you delist. SKU reduction is only worth doing as the admission price of a footprint decision, never as a saving in itself.
key.support: **What decides it, and it is $68m of released plant cost against $11m of surrendered revenue.** Profit is falling at 40% a year while sales fall at 8%: that five-to-one gap is fixed-cost leverage, and the fixed cost sits in three plants running at half utilization — the one large quantity on the page the client actually controls. Today production costs $136m: Chihuahua $20m + $18m = $38.0m, Grand Rapids $15m + $39.5m = $54.5m, Sayreville $18m + $25.5m = $43.5m. Per SKU the plants are not comparable: Chihuahua converts at $18m / 4,500 = $4k, Grand Rapids at $39.5m / 5,000 = $7.9k, Sayreville at $25.5m / 3,000 = $8.5k. Chihuahua's total SKU capacity is 4,500 + 7,500 = 12,000, which is 500 short of the 12,500 line. Consolidate everything into Chihuahua and production costs $20m + ($4k x 12,000) = $68m, a 50% cut, against $11m of revenue given up on the 500 SKUs that no longer fit at $22k each. Net +$57m, and pre-tax profit moves from $25m to $82m. The demand story stays exactly as the associate wrote it — it just is not the place to spend the team.
key.risks: Internal: implementation is a long-timeframe move and we do not yet know whether the two closing plants carry organized labour; distribution and warehousing need a built transition plan and purchasing has to move from local buying to a strong central function, and morale through a two-plant shutdown has to be managed or the $57m is eaten by delay. External: the consolidated plant still sells into a market falling 5% a year through a superstore channel that took 10 share points and is substituting private label, so the cost win buys time and a better balance sheet, not demand.
key.next: Two weeks on a closure and ramp plan, not on the channel: labour status and severance exposure at Grand Rapids and Sayreville, Chihuahua's ramp from 4,500 to 12,000 SKUs with the equipment and headcount it needs, and a SKU-level revenue cut to name which 500 SKUs go — then take the $82m number to the committee.

en: Minto: the first sentence is the verdict itself, an action with a subject. A correct verdict arriving after the facts fails this line.
Names the market decline, the superstore share gain, the 30% discount and the private label push as conditions the client cannot act on — and says so as the reason not to spend the two weeks there.
Puts the effort on the plant footprint and says it as an action on a named plant, not as a vague 'we should look at costs'.
Prices the trade with one number against the other: production cost released against revenue surrendered on the SKUs that no longer fit.
Uses the per-SKU conversion gap between the three plants to justify which plant survives, rather than keeping the largest or the domestic one.
Treats the SKU cut as the admission price of the consolidation, not as a standalone saving.
Gives one internal and one external risk.
ru: Минто: первое предложение — сам вердикт, действием и с субъектом. Верный вывод после фактов не засчитывается.
Называет падение рынка, +10 п.п. суперсторов, скидку 30% и подмену частной маркой условиями, на которые клиент не может воздействовать — и именно поэтому не тратит на них две недели.
Прикладывает усилие к производственному следу и говорит это действием по конкретному заводу, а не общим «надо посмотреть затраты».
Оценивает размен числом против числа: сколько производственных затрат высвобождается против того, сколько выручки отдаём на SKU, которые больше не помещаются.
Обосновывает, какой завод остаётся, разрывом в затратах на SKU между тремя площадками, а не тем, что он крупнейший или домашний.
Считает срез SKU платой за консолидацию, а не самостоятельной экономией.
Назван один внутренний и один внешний риск.

The plants convert differently — $4k per SKU at Chihuahua against $7.9k at Grand Rapids and $8.5k at Sayreville — and Chihuahua holds 12,000 SKUs of capacity against a 12,500 SKU line. Externally, the consolidated plant still sells into a market shrinking 5% a year through superstores that are pushing private label, so this buys margin and time, not demand. drills.anchor_metric: Порога в книге нет: цели по прибыли клиент не ставит, срока тоже. Единственная база для сравнения — текущая доналоговая прибыль $25m в год при выручке $275m. Значит вердикт нельзя закрыть фразой «проходим порог» — его надо считать против базы $25m.

mehanizm.naive: «Рынок упал, суперсторы забрали полку и режут цену на 30% — значит две недели уходят на канал: вернуть условия у суперсторов, перестроить прайс дилерам, защитить бренд от частной марки».
mehanizm.correct: Приложить усилие к производственному следу: три завода при 50% загрузки, свести всё в Chihuahua за $68m против $11m отданной выручки, прибыль $25m → $82m.
mehanizm.why: Величины, которые громче всего объясняют картину — падение рынка на 5% в год, +10 п.п. доли суперсторов, скидка 30%, подмена частной маркой — целиком лежат вне контура клиента; на них нельзя нажать, на них можно только реагировать. Книга прямо требует опознать макро как то, что вне контроля, и уйти в консолидацию заводов. Настоящий сигнал в записи — прибыль падает в пять раз быстрее выручки (-40% против -8%): это плечо постоянных затрат, а постоянные затраты сидят в трёх заводах при половинной загрузке, и вот это клиент двигает.

drills.family_note: круг 102: всё, что громко объясняет обвал прибыли — падение рынка на 5% в год, +10 п.п. доли суперсторов, скидка 30% дилерам, подмена частной маркой — лежит вне досягаемости клиента, а книга прямо печатает, что макро вне контроля и рычаг в производственном следе трёх заводов при 50% загрузки.
